title: API: Dedicated staged rollout endpoints (CRUD + approve/abort + status) w/ idempotency + audit event pagination
creator: Ethan Park
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Build the Dedicated staged rollout public control-plane API surface for operators (and later enterprise opt-in) to manage rollout plans on reserved pools.

This ticket covers:
- Dedicated rollout plan CRUD: create/update/get/list
- Approvals + abort endpoints (with audit event emission)
- Status endpoint used by Console + internal tooling
- Idempotency for write endpoints (create/update/approve/abort)
- Pagination for audit/event list endpoints (cursor-based)

Context
Dedicated pools are high-SLA, isolated GPU pools. Today we do pool-level “all-at-once” updates which can saturate a pool and violate latency/availability commitments. The staged rollout system introduces deterministic traffic weights per stage + gate evaluation + manual approvals. This ticket is the control-plane API contract for operators/Console, with strong safety/consistency guarantees.

Non-goals
- Implement gate evaluation logic (ENG-5124)
- Implement routing enforcement (ENG-5123)
- Implement Console UI (ENG-5126/5127)

API surface (proposal)
Base: /v1

1) Rollout Plans
- POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans
  Creates a new RolloutPlan attached to a Dedicated pool.
  Idempotent via Idempotency-Key header (required) and a request-scoped idempotency record keyed by (tenant_id, pool_id, idempotency_key).

- PATCH /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}
  Updates mutable fields (e.g., display name/description, stage definitions, gates, evaluation windows, auto-advance flags) using optimistic concurrency.
  Requires expected_plan_version to prevent lost updates.

- GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}
  Returns the plan spec + metadata.

- GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans?limit=&cursor=&status=
  List plans in a pool for Console list view and internal tooling.

2) Approvals / Abort
- POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}:approve
  Approves advancement from current stage -> next stage OR approves resuming from HOLD (depending on plan state machine).
  Requires permission rollout.approve.
  Idempotent via Idempotency-Key (required) + expected_plan_version.
  Emits audit event: dedicated_rollout.stage_approved.

- POST /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}:abort
  Aborts the rollout (enters ABORTED) and triggers routing to stop sending traffic to non-baseline variant (actual routing behavior handled elsewhere but this endpoint is the source of truth).
  Requires permission rollout.abort.
  Idempotent via Idempotency-Key (required) + expected_plan_version.
  Emits audit event: dedicated_rollout.aborted.

3) Status / Events
- GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}/status
  Returns computed state for Console:
  - current_stage_id, next_stage_id
  - stage states (PENDING/RUNNING/HOLD/FAILED/SUCCEEDED)
  - gate summaries (pass/fail/unknown, last_eval_at)
  - last_action + actor
  Notes: This endpoint may query the rollout orchestration/status aggregator service (ENG-5126/ENG-5124/ENG-5125) but the contract is defined here.

- GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}/events?limit=&cursor=
  Cursor-based pagination, stable ordering by (created_at, event_id) to avoid duplicates/misses.
  Used by Console “Audit trail” panel and to support compliance exports.

- GET /dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollout-plans/{plan_id}/events/{event_id}
  (Optional) Direct fetch used for deep links.

Request/response consistency requirements
- All write endpoints must support:
  - Idempotency-Key header (required)
  - Client-request-id field (optional but logged)
  - Safe retries on 5xx / timeouts without duplicating side effects

- Optimistic concurrency:
  - Update/approve/abort must include expected_plan_version
  - On mismatch return 409 conflict with latest plan_version and a human-readable error message

- Error codes:
  - 400 validation errors (invalid stage weights, missing required fields)
  - 401/403 for auth/RBAC
  - 404 for missing pool/plan
  - 409 for concurrency conflict
  - 412 for failed preconditions (e.g., approve when no next stage)

RBAC + tenancy
- Enforce tenant isolation: pool_id must belong to tenant context.
- Permissions (from ENG-5129/PR 28544):
  - rollout.edit for create/update
  - rollout.approve for approve
  - rollout.abort for abort
  - rollout.view for get/list/status/events

Audit logging
- Every state transition endpoint must emit an audit-style event (ENG-5128) with:
  actor_id, actor_type, tenant_id, pool_id, plan_id, plan_version, stage_id (when relevant), reason (optional), request_id/idempotency_key.
- Event list must be paginated and safe to query at high volume without unbounded scans.

Acceptance criteria
- Control-plane implements endpoints above (or a reviewed equivalent) with:
  - Idempotency-Key support on POST/PATCH/:approve/:abort
  - expected_plan_version checks for PATCH/:approve/:abort
  - Cursor-based pagination for list endpoints (plans + events)
  - RBAC enforcement for all endpoints
  - Structured audit events emitted for create/update/approve/abort
  - OpenAPI/SDK docs updated for internal operator usage

Test plan
- Unit tests:
  - Idempotency: same Idempotency-Key returns same response and does not duplicate approval/abort events
  - Concurrency: 409 on version mismatch
  - RBAC: deny approve/abort without permissions
  - Pagination: cursor stability and ordering

- Integration tests (can be partial in this ticket, full E2E in ENG-5132):
  - Create -> Update -> Approve -> Events list reflects actions in order

Notes / open questions
- Approve semantics: is approve always “advance to next stage” or can it also “resume current stage from HOLD”? Current leaning: approve is “allow advancement” and evaluator/orchestrator decides when to move; however Console expects a single approve CTA. Need final state machine alignment with Ethan/Mina.
- Abort vs Rollback: v1 endpoint is abort (stop rollout). Separate rollback endpoint may come later once we formalize baseline selection semantics.
- Events cursor format: base64-encoded "created_at|event_id" to ensure stable ordering.

comments: 2025-01-13 (Benji Okafor): Drafted initial endpoint shapes for create/update/get/list + events list. Requesting feedback from Chloe (Console backend) on status shape needed for UI. Also pinging Kaitlyn (RBAC) about new permission names and scopes for enterprise tenants.

2025-01-16 (Chloe Martin): Console needs a single status payload with per-stage gate summary (pass/fail/unknown) and current stage + whether an approval is required. Please avoid forcing the UI to join across plan + events for basic display. Fine with a dedicated /status endpoint.

2025-01-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): For RBAC we’re standardizing on rollout.view/edit/approve/abort. Ensure endpoints require rollout.view even for events. Also make sure tenant scoping is enforced by pool ownership and not by plan_id alone.

2025-01-23 (Ethan Park): Strong preference for cursor pagination on events (not offset) due to compliance exports and potential high event counts during incidents. Ordering should be deterministic with a tie-breaker (event_id).

2025-02-03 (Benji Okafor): Implemented CRUD endpoints with optimistic concurrency in control-plane. Added Idempotency-Key middleware and idempotency table keyed by (tenant_id, resource_scope, idempotency_key). Still finalizing approve/abort semantics with Jordan/Mina re: who advances stages vs orchestrator.

2025-02-10 (Jordan Lee): For determinism/safety, policy engine expects plan state transitions to be serialized. Approve should write an explicit ApprovalEvent and set plan 'approval_granted=true' for current stage, evaluator/orchestrator tick performs advancement. That keeps traffic allocation stable if multiple approves arrive concurrently.

2025-02-14 (Benji Okafor): Added events pagination and stable cursor (created_at,event_id). Added 409 conflict response including latest plan_version. Remaining: wire approve/abort to audit event emitter and ensure retries don’t double-emit.
2025-02-18 (Felix Schneider): Please include idempotency_key/request_id in the event payload returned by /events so Console can de-dupe and help SRE correlate with logs during incidents.
